# n-Dimensional and Hyper-surface Methods

Also called: n-Dimensional Isosurface Extraction, Hyper-surface Slicing, Dimension-Lifting Methods

## Overview
This family generalizes isosurface extraction from 3D spatial grids to $n$-dimensional domains (typically 4D, representing 3D space plus time or another parameter) by treating the isosurface as a hyper-surface within the higher-dimensional volume. It solves the problem of extracting topologically correct surfaces from high-dimensional scalar fields where standard 3D algorithms like [Marching Cubes](30-isosurface-extraction.md) fail due to combinatorial explosion or topological ambiguity. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by operating directly on $n$-dimensional hypercubes or simplices to define the surface geometry, rather than projecting 3D slices or using learning-based approximations.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on a discretized domain, typically a regular grid (Cartesian, octree, or tetrahedral) where each cell contains scalar values or occupancy states at its vertices or centers [G].

## Subtopics

### [High-Dimensional Triangulation Tables](1336-high-dimensional-triangulation-tables.md)
[High-Dimensional Triangulation Tables](1336-high-dimensional-triangulation-tables.md) generates lookup tables for isosurface extraction in $n$-dimensional hypercubes. It addresses the excessive simplex count produced by recursive contour-meshing by providing a direct generalization of Marching Cubes. It constructs a convex hull of edge midpoints and vertices within the hypercube, avoiding intermediate simplicial decomposition. This results in fewer triangles than extracting isosurfaces after simplicial decomposition. Choose this when a direct, exact lookup-based extraction in $n$-D is required and memory allows for the table size.

### [n-D Hyper-surface slicing](13583-n-d-hyper-surface-slicing.md)
[n-D Hyper-surface slicing](13583-n-d-hyper-surface-slicing.md) precomputes an $n$-dimensional hyper-surface (e.g., a tetrahedral grid in 4D) for a fixed iso-value, which is then interactively sliced along arbitrary hyperplanes to generate opaque 3D polygonal surfaces. It distinguishes itself by employing a lazy evaluation scheme that generates and caches cases on the fly, reducing computational and storage costs for infrequent configurations. Choose this for interactive visualization of time-varying 4D data where the iso-value is fixed during the precomputation phase.

### n-D Marching Cubes
- [S1, unofficial] 4D isosurface algorithms by Weigle and Banks and by Bhaniramka, Wenger, and Crawfis that generalize the Marching Cubes approach into n-D.

### Temporal Evolution Tracking
- [S2] A technique to track the evolution of isosurfaces (creation, splitting, merging) in volumetric and time-varying datasets using dimension-lifting.
- [S2] Generate hypercubic interval volume cases from 5-dimensional hypercubes.

### Ponchio and Hormann Interactive Multiresolution Volume Rendering
- [S2] An interactive multiresolution volume rendering algorithm for irregular time-varying datasets that extracts a 4D tetrahedral isosurface and converts it into dynamic triangles.
- [S2] Apply the algorithm by Bhaniramka et al. to extract a 4D tetrahedral isosurface from the dataset at full resolution.
- [S2] Apply the Batched Multi-Tessellation (BMT) algorithm to create a multi-resolution structure on the isosurface.
- [S2] Convert the faces of each tetrahedron in 4D space into dynamic triangles.
- [S2] Project the dynamic triangles in each patch into span space.
- [S2] Render the projected triangles on the GPU.
- [S2] Pre-processing time for a 3743 × 600 dataset takes more than 13 days.
- [S2] Rendering rate is 20M triangles/sec regardless of the input dataset after pre-processing.

## Background
The generalization of Marching Cubes to higher dimensions was proposed by Weigle and Banks [263] and Bhaniramka, Wenger, and Crawfis [13] [S1, unofficial]. These methods use a Marching Cubes-type approach to generalize into $n$-D. Dimension-lifting techniques have also been applied to track the evolution of isosurfaces, such as creation, splitting, and merging, in volumetric and time-varying datasets by generating hypercubic interval volume cases from 5-dimensional hypercubes [S2]. More recently, Ponchio and Hormann introduced an interactive multiresolution volume rendering algorithm for irregular time-varying datasets, extracting a 4D tetrahedral isosurface and converting it into dynamic triangles for GPU rendering [S2].
